clue.text: East African dress for one of Pooh's friends

definitions.meaning: a printed cotton cloth wrapped round the body, worn by women in Kenya and Tanzania
the mother kangaroo in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh stories

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a Swahili wrap garment and the kangaroo mother of Roo in the Hundred Acre Wood.

clue.text: Get rid of writer's trinketry

parts.note: to kick a habit is to get rid of it
the writer is George Bernard Shaw, so 'writer's' gives SHAW'S

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to throw out an author's collection of knick-knacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Kickshaws are trifles or fancy trinkets, so the collective sense is trinketry.

clue.text: The Union blockading American city

indicators.note: to blockade something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen

explanation.surface: A trade union holds a city in America under siege.
explanation.walkthrough: NAMUR is a city in Belgium; 'American city' suggests the US, but American only gives AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Namur is a Belgian city at the meeting of the Sambre and Meuse rivers.

clue.text: Resolute man, one proverbially industrious

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
the ant is the proverb's hard worker: 'Go to the ant, thou sluggard'

explanation.surface: A determined man described as hard-working by the old sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant is unshakeable in a decision, which is to be resolute.

clue.text: Continue to soak and wash

parts.note: good weather that holds continues
to water something is to wet or soak it

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions: keep the clothes soaking, then wash them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash' is not laundry here: an argument that won't wash is one that won't be accepted, the same as one that won't hold water.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean to stand up to scrutiny, as a plausible argument does.

clue.text: Bird who, in a speech, put poet down

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is put below the first
a speech is spoken, so the word who is spelt as it is pronounced

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like HOO
Edgar Allan Poe was an American poet

explanation.surface: A speaker who belittled a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with barred wings found across Europe, Asia and Africa.

clue.text: At first, like Arthur's father, an adherent of Protestantism

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word like is all that is used

parts.note: Uther Pendragon was King Arthur's father in legend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that King Arthur's father was originally a Protestant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lutheran follows the church founded on Martin Luther's teaching, a branch of Protestantism.

clue.text: His wife's departed with only half her jointure

definitions.text: His wife's departed with only half her jointure

parts.words: His wife's departed with only half her jointure
parts.note: a man whose spouse has died; a jointure is a widow's settlement, and taking only half of 'her' leaves ER to add to a widow

explanation.surface: A man whose wife has left him with only part of her estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests desertion and a divorce settlement; 'departed' means died, and the word for a bereaved wife plus half of 'her' gives the man.
explanation.definitionFit: A man whose spouse has died is the male counterpart of a widow.

clue.text: Steak that's cooked or not used

indicators.note: cooked as in falsified, so the letters of the phrase are reworked

explanation.surface: A steak described as either cooked or left untouched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' sits naturally with steak, but it rearranges OR NOT USED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos is a small round cut of beef fillet, a kind of steak.

clue.text: Beneath the surface of the river fish is swimming

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed below the first
in a down clue the surface of a word is its top, its first letter

parts.note: eels are fish

explanation.surface: Fish swim just under the surface of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' looks like what the fish do, but a head that is swimming reels with dizziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling means feeling giddy, as when one's head is spinning.

clue.text: Happen to change tack

definitions.meaning: of a sailing boat, to turn onto the opposite tack

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occur in general use, and in sailing it means turn the bow through the wind.

clue.text: Leader capturing one point or two?

indicators.note: the leader holds the other piece inside himself as a captive

parts.note: Il Duce, 'the leader', was Mussolini's title
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A team captain winning a point or two.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tennis scoring, where deuce is also used, but the definition is the plain number: a deuce is a two in cards or dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A deuce is a card or die face showing the number two.

clue.text: A spring-sown seed will flourish and branch out

indicators.note: flourishing growth reshapes these letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener's promise that seed sown in spring will grow and put out branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch out' fits the plant picture, but it is the definition, the figurative sense of venturing into new things.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to start doing new and wider things, as a fledgling leaves the nest.

clue.text: Clever design of statue

indicators.note: a design is an arrangement, so the letters of statue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark admiring a well-designed statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and quick-witted.

clue.text: Two prizes put up by society's leaders

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a reward is a prize
a pot is a prize, as in a trophy cup

explanation.surface: A society awards two prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer describes the highest social class, the elite.

clue.text: Sounding worried — an old and crabby woman

indicators.note: sounding means the word is spelt as it is pronounced

parts.note: harried means harassed or worried
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumpy old woman who comes across as anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bad-tempered, scolding older woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Calf seen around Trenton?

definitions.meaning: a newborn cow of the Jersey breed, read as new plus Jersey
the US state whose capital is Trenton

explanation.definitionFit: A young Jersey cow is a fresh one of that breed, and the state is the one with Trenton as capital.

clue.text: Dark brown animal caught in trap? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, as prey is caught
the roles are swapped, so the trap goes inside the animal rather than the other way round

parts.note: a brute is a beast
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A brown animal ensnared, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunette means having dark brown hair, so the colour sense is dark brown.

clue.text: Blue poetess mistaking passion for love

indicators.note: one letter is taken in error for another, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: Sappho was a Greek poetess
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A depressed poetess confusing desire with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests a sad Sappho, but it defines the gem colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a deep bright blue, the colour of the gemstone.

clue.text: Miffed, went on ahead — and went fast

parts.note: miffed is offended, hurt
someone who led went in front of the others

explanation.surface: An offended person stormed off ahead at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle is to rush along at great speed.

clue.text: City witnessed first fighting

indicators.note: first signals that the fighting piece comes before the other

parts.note: war is fighting
saw means witnessed

explanation.surface: A city that saw fighting before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Examination given to gold, I hear …

parts.note: an audit is an examination of accounts
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An inspection of gold reserves, so I am told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a link to the next clue, but it defines the answer: an auditor is a hearer, from Latin audire.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is literally a listener, one who hears.

clue.text: … in general, it must be the acid test

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Generally, this must be the decisive trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A litmus test is a decisive test, and litmus paper literally tests for acid.

clue.text: Admiral in bowler

parts.note: an Elizabethan admiral famous for finishing his game of bowls before facing the Armada

explanation.surface: A naval commander wearing a bowler hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowler suggests a hat or a cricketer; here it is a player of bowls, a lawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan seaman was a vice-admiral against the Spanish Armada and a keen bowls player.

clue.text: Jack's mackerel bait

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme Jack who could eat no fat, and the small fish in the saying about catching a mackerel

explanation.surface: Bait that Jack uses to catch mackerel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is the nursery rhyme man, and 'a sprat to catch a mackerel' is a small outlay to win a big prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The small herring-like fish is the surname of the rhyme's Jack and the bait of the proverb.

clue.text: A light bearing 90" (or 270)

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A navigation light seen on a bearing of ninety degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 90" is 90 degrees; at ninety or two hundred and seventy degrees from the bow, something lies at right angles to the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam means at right angles to the keel, directly off either side of a ship.

clue.text: Carelessly lower wheel on foot

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters of the word fall out of order

explanation.surface: Someone lowers a wheel onto a foot without care.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the spiked revolving disc on a rider's spur, worn on the heel.

clue.text: Office worker with curly hair, an alluring woman

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
a tress is a lock or curl of hair

explanation.surface: A curly-haired office temp who is very attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptress is a seductive woman who entices.

clue.text: Dissenter punished by fatigue

indicators.note: punished means roughly treated, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel is penalised with exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue is weariness, the state of being worn out.

clue.text: Odd game

definitions.meaning: strange or peculiar, in British slang
a card game of melding sets and runs

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for peculiar and also names a card game.
